s: The church is established by God among the fathers after deliverance from bondage, then more fully among the people of Nephi as they remember their duty. It spreads throughout the land, bringing many baptisms, continual peace, the Lord's blessings, and no inequality.

l: inequality, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: exists_among people of Nephi [some lifted themselves up while others served the needy] Alma saw great inequality among the people. Some lifted themselves up in pride and despised and neglected the needy, while others abased themselves and gave substance and aid to those in need.

l: contentions among the people of the church, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: include envyings [and strife, malice, persecutions, and pride] Great contentions arose among the people of the church in the eighth year. They included envyings, strife, malice, persecutions, and pride exceeding that of those outside the church.

l: destruction of the people, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_brought_on_by wickedness of the church [through the example of the church] Alma saw that the church’s example was leading unbelievers from one piece of iniquity to another, thus bringing on the destruction of the people.

l: appointment of Nephihah as chief judge, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_given_by Alma (son of Alma) [according to the voice of the people] Alma selected Nephihah, a wise man among the elders of the church, and gave him power according to the voice of the people. Nephihah was appointed chief judge to enact and enforce laws and to judge and govern the people.

l: Alma's relinquishment of the judgment-seat, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: transfers judgment-seat [to Nephihah] At the commencement of the ninth year, Alma delivered the judgment-seat to Nephihah. Alma did not relinquish the high priesthood, which he retained for himself.

l: preaching of the word, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Preaching of the word is a divinely guided ministry performed by Alma, Ammon, Aaron, their brethren, and others according to revelation and prophecy. It is presented as more powerful in leading people to just conduct than the sword, so Alma uses it to reclaim the people of Nephi and the Zoramites through pure testimony against pride, craftiness, and contention. Aaron, Ammon, and their brethren persist through rejection and imprisonment while preaching across cities, houses of worship, and among the Lamanites and Amalekites. Their teaching brings thousands of Lamanites to knowledge of the Lord and repentance among many Zoramites. The word is preached in synagogues, houses, and streets, delivered by angels, and given to men, women, and little children. It concludes with instruction that teaching continue diligently, temperately, boldly, humbly, lovingly, and with self-control.

l: Abinadi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Abinadi is a holy prophet who delivers the word of God and speaks of Jesus Christ, redemption, and the priests’ seed. Alma’s father believes his words. Abinadi dies by fire for belief in God; afterward, his words about the priests’ seed are fulfilled.

l: children of men, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The children of men are fallen and lost because of Adam’s fall, must die, and will be judged before God according to mortal deeds. They can receive glad tidings through angels and are invited to repentance. Alma teaches them to remember captivity and deliverance, seek a mighty change of heart, be baptized, follow the good shepherd, resist the adversary, pray, obey commandments, receive the word of the Son, and, by repenting without hardening their hearts, enter God’s rest.

l: Alma's fathers, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Alma's fathers were freed from king Noah’s people, enslaved by the Lamanites, then delivered through God’s word; they humbled themselves, trusted, endured faithfully, changed their hearts, and were saved.

l: people of king Noah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: hold Alma's father [in their hands before deliverance] The people of king Noah held Alma's fathers in their hands before Alma's fathers were delivered by the mercy and power of God.

l: the wicked, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The wicked are those who persist in iniquity, pride, envy, persecution, costly apparel, riches, and neglect of the poor and needy, choosing evil works over good. Unless they repent, they are excluded from the righteous and cast into fire. Because of their iniquity, the devil leads them captive; after death their spirits enter outer darkness without the Spirit of the Lord, where they weep, wail, and gnash teeth. They remain miserable until resurrection, then face God’s wrath and partake of the bitter fruits of evil works.

l: the righteous, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The righteous are people whose garments are cleansed and spotless and whose works meet repentance. Their prayers preserve the people in the land from immediate destruction. Their names are written in the book of life, and after death they enter paradise, rest from trouble and sorrow, are reunited with their bodies, shine in God’s kingdom, and receive an inheritance at God’s right hand.

l: devil, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The devil is a shepherd of those who reject the good shepherd, leading followers to evil works and death. He captivates and takes captive people who harden their hearts until they know nothing of God’s mysteries. Through cunning plans, he ensnares hearts and contributes to inequality. He influences deception, including Zeezrom’s plan, and deceives Korihor by appearing as an angel and teaching him there is no God. An enemy to all righteousness, he works to destroy the children of God and may overpower those not watchful unto prayer. Those who delay repentance until death become his subjects; he enters the wicked, takes possession of their house, and leads them by his will. After the church is established throughout the land, it overcomes him.

l: the good shepherd's sheep, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: belong_to the good shepherd [by hearkening to his voice] The good shepherd's sheep hearken to his voice and follow him. The good shepherd calls them into his fold and commands that no ravenous wolf be allowed to enter among them.

l: Zarahemla, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Zarahemla is a city and land central to the church, government, war, and migration. A church is established there, Alma speaks to its people, and brethren have faced an awful dilemma there. After peace, it receives prisoners and surviving men while sending two thousand men to support Helaman. Pahoran serves there as chief judge and governor, but rebels take the city, appoint a king, and ally with the Lamanites; Pahoran and Moroni plan to retake it for food. Later, men with their wives and children depart from Zarahemla for the land northward.

l: land of Mormon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_a land [in the borders of Nephi] The land of Mormon was within the borders of Nephi, and Alma's father established a church there and baptized his brethren in its waters.

l: wilderness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The Lamanites travel through the wilderness around the head of the river Sidon to reach Manti. Moroni sends spies into the wilderness and hides part of his army there.

l: kingdom of heaven, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The kingdom of heaven is near and soon at hand, proclaimed as the Lord calls people to repent. It cannot be inherited by those who refuse repentance, are unprepared, are not born again, remain wicked, or are unclean. The righteous, prepared and clothed in spotless garments, may enter it, remain there, and have eternal life.

l: hell, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Hell contains chains that encircle souls; it binds hardened people captive to the devil toward destruction, yet Alma’s fathers were loosed through faith and changed hearts.

l: tree of life, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The tree of life is in the garden of Eden, where its fruit could provide everlasting life. After the Fall it was guarded by cherubim and a flaming sword, preventing partaking until there was a space for repentance. Those who come to God, repent, come to Christ, and nourish the word with an eye of faith may partake of its fruit and receive life forever.

l: gospel invitation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: invites the people [to repent and be received] The gospel invitation is extended to all men through the call to repent and come to God. Those who come may freely partake of the bread and waters of life and bring forth works of righteousness.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Repentance is required for salvation, eternal life, mercy, cleansing, being received by God, inheriting the kingdom of heaven, and avoiding destruction and the Lord’s fierce anger. It is to be declared with the plan of redemption and preached to every people. Alma repeatedly urges people to repent quickly, beginning in this life rather than delaying until death; procrastination leaves the wicked subject to the spirit of the devil. Those who repent, find mercy, and endure to the end are saved, and repentance can bring knowledge of the Lord, birth of God, and joy. Alma, Amulek, the sons of Mosiah, and others preach it throughout the land, including to Ammonihah, the Lamanites, Zoramites, and individuals. Ammonihah rejects repentance and faces anger, while many Zoramites repent but are driven from their land and receive an inheritance in Jershon. Anti-Nephi-Lehi experience sore repentance and fear taking up arms. Alma labors to bring souls to repentance and joy, and a son is commanded to repent, forsake sins, return, and acknowledge his faults.

l: salvation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Salvation is deliverance promised to the righteous and to those who believe on the name of the Son of God. It requires humility, trust in the true and living God, faith, repentance, and faithfulness until the end; the truly penitent receive it, while those who do not repent are cast off. It cannot come through the law of Moses, nor can people be saved in their sins, because no unclean thing inherits the kingdom of heaven. It comes only through the Lord Jesus Christ, his power and deliverance, the last sacrifice, the atonement, and the plan of mercy. Salvation brings people from death, misery, darkness, and destruction into everlasting light. It is anticipated for righteous people who are slain and go to God, proclaimed as glad tidings, and presented as available now. The ministry prepares people for it, while records and words bring knowledge of God and aid the salvation of souls. God also brings about the salvation of many souls through small means.

l: mighty change of heart, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_experienced_by the people [through spiritual rebirth] A mighty change of heart was wrought in Alma's father and in his fathers after they believed, humbled themselves, and trusted in God. Alma asks whether the people have experienced this change and whether they can still feel to sing the song of redeeming love.

l: judgment, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Judgment follows temporal death and the reuniting of soul and body. God, Christ, and the Holy Spirit conduct it at the bar of Christ the Son. All people stand before God and are judged according to the deeds done in the mortal body: their works, words, thoughts, and whether those works were good or evil. They must acknowledge that God’s judgments are just, while the deaths of the innocent witness against those responsible. People are asked whether they can look up with pure hearts, clean hands, and God’s image upon their countenances; righteous judgment is restored to righteous judges.

l: death, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Death is a binding, sorrow-causing force associated with the devil’s wages for evil works and separation from good. People are encircled by its bands, and widespread death and destruction bring mourning and contrasting eternal outcomes. Yet God’s power and the Son of God’s death break and loose death’s bands; Christ’s death atones for sins and promises resurrection. This hope changes the people of Ammon’s response: they do not fear death and will suffer it rather than fight their brethren. The records end by contrasting endless wo for some dead with never-ending happiness at God’s right hand for others.

l: chains of hell, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Chains of hell are captivity by the devil: hardened hearts lose knowledge of God’s mysteries, leading to bondage and destruction; only God can deliver people from such captivity.

l: blood of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: cleanses garments [from every stain] The blood of Christ cleanses garments from every stain. Alma teaches that garments must be purified through this blood for a person to be saved.

l: garments, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: must_be white [to be saved] Garments must be washed white and cleansed from all stain. Alma asks whether the people have had their garments cleansed and made white through the blood of Christ.

l: sin, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Sin is transgression, iniquity, rebellion, and wickedness that brings spiritual death, condemnation, God’s wrath, eternal torment, and loss of the kingdom of God when it is not repented of. It is especially abominable before God, and the sanctified view it with abhorrence. Alma fasts over the people’s sins, recalls his own torment and harmful rebellion, and warns that sin has led people toward destruction. The Lamanite converts reject their former violence and fear returning to sin, while the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi seek refuge after their sins and murders. Throughout, people are commanded to lay aside, cast off, forsake, and repent of every sin. Jesus Christ takes away the sins of those who steadfastly believe on his name, and the Son of God suffers and dies to atone for and blot out the transgressions of his people.

l: pride, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: prevents_preparation meeting God [when a person is not stripped of pride] Alma warns that people must be stripped of pride to be prepared to meet God. Those who are puffed up in pride and set their hearts on the vain things of the world must repent.

l: kingdom of the devil, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: It is inherited by those raised to endless misery.

l: the city of Gideon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Gideon is a city built in the valley of Gideon, named for the man Nehor slew with a sword.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Repentance is presented as necessary for salvation, inheriting the kingdom of God, avoiding destruction, condemnation, and perishing, and entering the rest of God or the Lord. Through faith in Jesus Christ, repentance can bring redemption, remission of sins, mercy, sanctification, righteous fruit, knowledge of God’s mysteries, release from darkness and the pains of hell, and hope of eternal life. It is commanded and preached by Helaman, Alma, Melchizedek, Aaron, and Ammon. Aaron teaches the king to repent of all sins and call on God in faith, despite an Amalekite’s challenge. The people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi repent of sins and murders, while many Lamanites repent after witnessing a massacre. Repentance is granted in the probationary state, claimed by mercy, and requires sin and punishment; people are urged not to delay it or harden their hearts.

l: redemption, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Redemption is the great and eternal plan laid from the foundation of the world. It provides the resurrection of the dead and, through the Son of God’s sacrifice, repentance, and atonement, reclaims mankind from spiritual death and offers mercy to those who repent and believe on his name. It was anticipated in preparatory redemption, taught as people looked forward to the Son, and proclaimed among the Lamanites. It does not destroy justice: the wicked and those who do iniquity remain as though no redemption had been made, except for the loosing of the bands of death.

l: Helaman's father, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Helaman's father, a person confined to the judgment-seat, addresses beloved brethren with testimony and calls to repentance, faith, baptism, and obedience; later he entrusts sacred things to Helaman and commands diligent preaching and reliance on God.

l: beloved brethren, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Beloved brethren are urged to humble themselves, repent, be baptized, keep commandments, and walk blamelessly; they show faith and righteousness.

l: brethren at Zarahemla, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_established_in way of his righteousness [again] The brethren at Zarahemla experienced much affliction and sorrow but were established again in the way of righteousness.

l: Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The Lord is God, creator of the earth, heavens, and all people, who dwells in heaven with holy angels and knows the thoughts and intents of the heart. He is merciful, hears prayer, extends his arm to those who repent and believe on his name, and is Redeemer of all men. He also judges sin without allowance, gives commandments, counsels and teaches nations in their own tongues, and brings justice and judgment upon the wicked. Across the records, the Lord calls, directs, and strengthens people for his work. He calls people through angels, commands the sons of Mosiah to establish his word among the Lamanites, comforts them by his Spirit, and makes them instruments for the salvation of many souls. He grants power to Alma and Amulek according to faith in Christ, sends an angel to Amulek, permits preaching and repentance, and does not allow Alma and Amulek to be burned before their work is finished. He heals according to faith, reveals where captives will be delivered, pours out his Spirit to prepare people for the word, and begins his work among the Lamanites. The Lord delivers people from bondage, captivity, enemies, prison, bonds, and death; preserves the faithful; and commands the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi to leave so they will not perish. He receives women, children, and those consumed by fire into glory after death, blesses souls forever, and gives the righteous rest. Yet he permits the righteous to be slain so that justice may come upon the wicked, and he will not spare those who refuse to repent.

l: Redeemer, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The Redeemer lives and comes among his people; Lamoni says he has seen him, and declares that he will come forth, be born of a woman, and redeem all mankind who believe on his name.

l: Son of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The Son of God is a person: the son of the Father, also identified as the Eternal Father of heaven, earth, and all things in them. He is full of grace, equity, and truth, and his coming, sufferings, death, and resurrection are taught, foretold, declared, and testified of. He comes upon earth and into the world, is born of Mary at Jerusalem, and suffers pains, afflictions, temptations of every kind, infirmities, sins, transgressions, and death according to the flesh. These sufferings enable deliverance: he takes upon himself the sins and transgressions of his people and of those who believe on his name, atoning for sins and blotting out transgressions through his power. Through his atonement and redemption, the repentant can receive mercy and remission of sins, while he does not save people in their sins. He rises from the dead, causes resurrection, appears to people after his resurrection, and will judge the resurrected and all people. His role throughout is to redeem mankind and God's people from their sins.

l: Mary, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_a virgin [precious and chosen vessel] Mary is described as a virgin and a precious, chosen vessel who will conceive by the power of the Holy Ghost and bring forth the Son of God.
